narrative: A Syrian man traveling with his wife and four children was on a vessel carrying 91 people that set out from Turkey toward Italy and ran into trouble on 9 October 2016, before being rescued off the Greek island of Milos. The family was taken to a reception center on the island of Leros, where all of them formally registered their intention to seek asylum in Greece. The request was ignored. They were held without access to a lawyer or the UN refugee agency despite several requests. On 19 October police took 13 people from the camp to the police station and told them they would be transferred to Athens. The next morning they were taken to the island of Kos, refused food despite the young children and babies in the group, and again told they would be flown to Athens. They were instead flown, under the escort of European border-agency officers, to Adana in Turkey, believing until they landed that they were going to Athens. One of them said later: 'When I saw the Turkish flag at the airport, my dreams were shattered.'
